name: vehicle-driver-assignment-visual
description: Visual check (#921 retarget): a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now — a qualified, idle employee boards a free vehicle of the right role on their own the moment a vehicle-gated task needs one (VehicleReservation.ts / ArrivalGate.resolveBoarding / VehicleBoarding.ts's requestBoardVehicle). Player-facing driver assignment/unassignment is gone: no click anywhere in this file's own role:'player' steps targets an Assign/Unassign control, and no step issues the console-only `vehicle driver` command (that command still exists — assignDriver/unassignDriver are called directly by the automatic reservation/boarding path itself — but nothing here calls it manually). Buys a drill_rig, hires and licenses a driller, orders a drill plan (drill_hole is a vehicle-gated PendingAction requiring the drill_rig role, same gate #553 put on drilling), and watches the vehicle get itself a driver as the holes actually land.

steps.description: cash:100000 funds the drill_rig ($35,000) and the driller hire ($1,000) bought/hired below, with headroom left over for payroll/fuel/maintenance while the automatic claim-and-drill sequence runs its real course.
drill_rig, not debris_hauler: drill_plan's own PendingActions carry requiredVehicleRole:'drill_rig' (Drill.ts), so this is the role the automatic claim below actually needs to exercise.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- hiring a driller only grants the 'blasting' starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION, Employee.ts), never the driving.drill_rig licence a drill_rig needs. This grants it directly so the scenario doesn't also have to build and staff a driving_center just to reach the licence -- the player-facing path for a real game is `employee train` at a driving_center, exercised elsewhere (tutorial-interactive.json's own train-driller step).

expect.note: employee #1's starting blasting(1) + this grant's driving.drill_rig(1) = 2

steps.description: Vehicles panel is already open from the buy step above (#411) -- this is a pure observation beat, capturing the baseline before-claim state: one drill_rig, driver:none.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:10,10
steps.description: Queues the vehicle-gated task: drill_plan orders 9 drill_hole PendingActions, each with requiredVehicleRole:'drill_rig' (Drill.ts) -- none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after this confirms. 10,10 to 16,16 at the tool's own default 3m spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) computes exactly the declared 3x3 grid (round(6/3)+1 = 3 per side), so no spacing-stepper click is needed before dragging.

No pollable summary field exposes a vehicle's driverId (state-schema-definitions.ts only tracks counts, never a specific vehicle's own fields), so this is a fixed pad rather than a wait_until, same tradeoff blast-drill-plan-ui.json's own 'tick 40' partial-drilling step makes for the same reason. Sandbox-measured: by tick 30 the driller has already claimed drill_rig #1, walked to it, and boarded (driver:#1), still short of the first hole landing -- the very next observe step's `vehicle list` output is expected to show driver:#1, proving the automatic claim already happened well before any hole completes.

Mid-course state: driver:#1 -- the driller has claimed and boarded drill_rig #1 entirely on their own, before the first hole has even landed. No summary field carries a specific vehicle's driverId for `expect` to check programmatically (state-schema-definitions.ts), so this step's proof is the command output and screenshot themselves, for the visual channel to inspect.

No click, no `vehicle driver` command -- the driller (licensed above) claims and reserves the free drill_rig, walks to it, boards, drives to each ordered hole, and drills it entirely on their own (VehicleReservation.ts / ArrivalGate.resolveBoarding). holeCount can only ever reach 9 once every hole has actually been drilled by a driver who genuinely boarded the vehicle -- there is no other path that lands a hole, so this is itself the proof the automatic claim worked, not just that ticking didn't crash.

Final state: driver:none again -- releaseVehicleOnCompletion (VehicleReservation.ts) dismounts the driver and frees the vehicle once the last hole's PendingAction completes and nothing else claims it, the same release the fully-automatic vehicles.integration.test.ts coverage already pins at the unit/integration layer. All 9 holes landing (holeCount:9, checked by the wait_until step above) is what actually proves the automatic claim worked all the way through -- not this step, which only shows the far side of the same cycle.
